extracted.intended_audience: general public, journalists, and stakeholders (consumers and policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: A government press release from a state attorney general announcing enforcement results (settlements/penalties) stemming from an investigation into fraudulent activity affecting regulatory rulemaking. Focuses on factual findings, outcomes, and official statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline / Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney General James Secures $615,000 from Companies that Supplied Fake Comments to Influence FCC’s Repeal of Net Neutrality Rules
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the main actor, the enforcement outcome, and the key subject (amount, companies, and the policy at issue) so readers immediately grasp the significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadline / Summary Strap
rubrics_metrics.description: Three Companies Supplied Fake Comments to FCC Impersonating Millions of Americans Without Their Knowledge or Consent to Influence Internet Policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a concise second-line summary that amplifies the headline with the core wrongdoing and scale; reinforces the news hook for readers and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date and Dateline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear publication date and location at the top of the release to establish timeliness and jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Paragraph: Clear Statement of Outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: New York Attorney General Letitia James today secured $615,000 from three companies, LCX, Lead ID, and Ifficient, that supplied millions of fake public comments to influence a 2017 proceeding by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to repeal net neutrality rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a succinct paragraph that states who took action, what was achieved (settlement/penalty), the parties involved, and the broader issue — avoid burying the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation / Definition of Technical Terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Net neutrality prohibits broadband providers from blocking, slowing down, or charging companies to prioritize certain content on the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the subject involves policy or technical terms, include a brief plain-language definition so non-specialist readers understand the stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of Investigation and Link to Supporting Report
rubrics_metrics.description: An investigation by the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) found that the fake comments used the identities of millions of consumers...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which office conducted the investigation and, where available, link to or reference a report that documents findings for credibility and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations from Principal Official(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Public comment opportunities are a chance for Americans to give their input on important government policies, and these companies abused that for their own selfish purposes,” said Attorney General James.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short, pointed quote from the lead official that expresses intent, summarizes the significance, and provides a human voice or policy stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Factual Details and Scale of Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: More than 8.5 million fake comments that impersonated real people were submitted to the FCC, and more than half a million fake letters were sent to Congress. LCX and Lead ID each fabricated responses for 1.5 million consumers. Ifficient supplied more than 840,000 fake responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete numbers, timelines, and specific behaviors to convey the scope and mechanics of the wrongdoing; specificity strengthens the newsworthiness and evidentiary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakdown of Enforcement Terms (Penalties & Disgorgement)
rubrics_metrics.description: LCX and its principals will pay $400,000 in penalties and disgorgement to New York and $100,000 to the San Diego District Attorney’s Office. Lead ID and its principal will pay $30,000 to New York. Ifficient will pay $63,750 to New York, and $21,250 to Colorado.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List settlement amounts and recipients clearly and itemize by defendant where applicable so the outcome is transparent and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Context and Cross-Agency Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The fraud... infected other government proceedings as well. ... more than 1 million fake comments were generated for other rulemaking proceedings, and more than 3.5 million fake digital signatures for letters and petitions were generated for federal and state legislators and government officials across the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain wider consequences beyond the single matter — linkage to other proceedings, systemic patterns, or industry practices helps explain public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of Cooperative Partners / Jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OAG wishes to thank the offices of the Attorney General of Colorado and the San Diego District Attorney for their assistance in this matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name other agencies or offices that assisted to reflect collaboration and interjurisdictional coordination; useful for both transparency and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Responsible Staff and Organizational Units
rubrics_metrics.description: This matter was handled by Senior Enforcement Counsel Jordan Adler and former Assistant Attorney General Noah Stein of the Bureau of Internet and Technology, under the supervision of Deputy Bureau Chief Clark Russell and Bureau Chief Kim Berger. The Bureau... is a part of the Division for Economic Justice...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names of counsel/staff and organizational context (bureaus/divisions) handling the matter to show accountability and point of contact; can also indicate expertise and internal structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation of Enforcement Mission / Public Reassurance
rubrics_metrics.description: “No one should have their identity co-opted by manipulative companies... We will always fight to ensure that consumers’ identities are protected and fraudulent companies are stopped.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include language that articulates the agency’s enforcement commitment and reassures the public that action will continue; this reinforces policy goals and public trust.
